newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK TEXTILE GROUP PINS HOPES ON EUROPEAN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: TURK TEXTILE GROUP PINS HOPES ON EUROPEAN MARKET.

text.p: Turkish textile group Sonmez Holding A.S., suffering a decline in profits this year, hopes that European markets will revive in 1997, a senior company official said.

"The (European) markets are stagnant and we are working on a very low profit margin just to sell our products. But we believe recession in Europe will turn to a reinvigoration next year and recovery will be seen in the textile sector," Baki Meric, Sonmez's financial coordinator, told Reuters.
"We chose to produce at full capacity and sell all of our output at lower prices in the face of falling demand, instead of reducing production," Meric said of this year's performance.
"Our direct exports this year will decrease 10 percent from last year's $70 million which represents 10 to 15 percent of our total yarn sales and 30 percent of our total fabric sales," Meric said.
"But we are dependent on export markets because our domestic sales are also to the exporter-producers."

The group's Sonmez Filament Sentetik Iplik ve Elyaf Sanayi has a production capacity of 30,000 tonnes of polyester yarn per year and had a 90 percent capacity utilisation rate (CUR) in the first nine months of 1996.

Sonmez Pamuklu Sanayii, with a 16,000-tonne annual output capacity of cotton yarn and fabric, had 80 percent CUR in the same period. Another group firm is ASF Iplik, Dokuma ve Boya Sanayi which has a yearly fabric weaving capacity of 45 million squaremetres and 70 percent CUR in January-September.
Sonmez Filament shares closed steady at 9,200 lira on Tuesday and Sonmez Pamuklu shares fell 50 lira to 3,950.
Sonmez Filament raised its sales 34 percent to 2.21 trillion lira in first half 1996 from 1.65 trillion in the same 1995 period, while its net profit melted down to 45 billion lira from 215 billion.
First half sales of Sonmez Pamuklu surged 77 percent to 2.07 trillion lira from 1.17 trillion a year ago with net profits shrinking to 192 billion lira from 252 billion.
Meric said they would soon break the ground for their joint power producing venture Entek Elektrik Uretimi with industrial Koc Holding conglomerate.
"A contractor company will be chosen by mid-October and we will begin to use our own electricity before mid-1997," he said.

Entek power plant to be owned 80 percent by the Koc group and 20 percent by Sonmez, will be built just beside the group's three textile plants and leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi, a Koc-Fiat joint-venture in the western Bursa town.
The $100 million plant with 100 MegaWatt power generation capacity, will meet all electricity needs of the four companies. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
